what: aide-memory source-protection scope INCLUDES hooks, not just the core engine. User intent from the outset was "minimize ability for people to get source code" — and hooks (both .sh bash files AND .js node helpers that call into the memory engine) are source code that ships with the package. In the 0.3.0 release I bundled only the three core entries (dist/cli/aide-memory.js, dist/memory/index.js, dist/memory/cli.js) and left scripts/hooks/*.sh + *.js unbundled and readable. That was an implementation shortcut I made without surfacing the tradeoff to the user. The correct standard for any future release is: hook logic must also be hidden via either (a) bundling each .js helper into dist/hooks/<name>.js AND migrating bash-script logic into JS so .sh files become thin shims, or (b) consolidating hook logic into `aide-memory hook <name>` CLI subcommands with .sh files reducing to single-line `exec aide-memory hook <name>`. Option (b) is the architecturally cleanest answer and matches the original binary-plan Phase 3 approach. Bash shims remain visible either way (bash has no compile) but they reduce to trivial glue. Apply this retroactively in a 0.3.1 or 0.4.0 release.
why: User corrected me 2026-04-21 after 0.3.0 publish: hooks being visible in shipped tarball violated the source-protection goal. I should have caught this during the audit (memory 158) but treated "minified bundles clean" as sufficient. Locking in that hooks are in scope so future sessions / refactors don't make the same shortcut.
